quote.text: Promises and pie-crust are made to be broken.
quote.author: Jonathan Swift, Polite Conversation, 1738

stories.headline: Araghchi offers to reopen Hormuz in seven days; UKMTO logs 23 attacks
stories.dek: Iran’s foreign minister put the first number of days on the table in Baghdad on Saturday. Lloyd’s List counted 477 transits in September — the strait’s busiest month of the war.

stories.headline: ASSA ABLOY bought Sargent & Greenleaf in December 2025 and now lists 174 brands
stories.dek: Sold Secure’s live register grades a Mul-T-Lock padlock Silver and a Squire closed-shackle Diamond. A Yale and an Abloy are the same company and not the same object.

stories.headline: Apple opened iPhone Duo pre-orders in Singapore at S$3,099 and sold out
stories.dek: Shipping estimates slipped to around 25 January within half an hour. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman: “Apple made a major mistake here.”

stories.headline: NEA logs PSI 93 in the north at 5am, down from Sunday’s 230
stories.dek: Three of the seven Indonesian firms served under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act got materially identical notices in 2015. The Act allows S$100,000 a day; nothing has ever been collected.

stories.headline: China drafts export curbs on open-weight AI models above two trillion parameters
stories.dek: The 16 October draft covers forty technologies and keeps the open-source carve-out — as an automatic licence Beijing can revoke. Comments close on 15 November.

stories.headline: Oris relaunches the ProPilot Calibre 111 with a ten-day hand-wound movement
stories.dek: CHF 6,100 on the steel bracelet, 43mm across and 13.2mm thick, with 240 hours of running from a mainspring 1.8 metres long. No Singapore price yet.

stories.headline: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary opens at Metascore 99 and $15m
stories.dek: “You Can See Everything” took $15m from 855 screens against Street Fighter’s $31m from 3,575 — twice the take per screen, for a film of two hours fifty-four.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Lancet Series
stories.headline: NUS researchers co-wrote the Lancet’s new paper on children’s digital media
stories.dek: Published 4 October, it models 2.8 million healthy years lost to depression. Professor Alan Woodward counters that 71 per cent of the 121 underlying reviews were rated low quality.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Paradox Day
stories.headline: American producer prices rose 1.3% in September and the Treasury 30-year yield fell
stories.dek: Brent gained 9.6 per cent in seven sessions to $109.86 while the US 10-year fell 15 basis points to 5.09 — the third consecutive issue it has fallen by exactly that.

stories.headline: Nishikigoi exports from Japan reached 9.97 billion yen in 2025, up 37.9 per cent
stories.dek: China’s imports rose 724.6 per cent in a single year. Of roughly 200,000 carp spawned, Japan’s own transport ministry says 500 to 1,000 reach adulthood.

stories.headline: Alzheimer’s & Dementia finds 7.2 years of cognitive health between the extremes
stories.dek: 54,217 people across China, the United States, England and Korea. Training hard and staying social are not substitutes for each other: the hazard ratio between them is 1.01.

stories.headline: Kenshi Yonezu’s Singapore tickets go on general sale at noon on Thursday
stories.dek: SIX60’s presales open today and tomorrow, with general sale on Wednesday. The Kyushu Basho is already sold out on all fifteen days.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank logged record remittances of $35.6bn; the kerb market explains the surge
stories.dek: Monthly inflows have fallen below $3bn and the kerb dollar trades at Tk128 against a bank rate of Tk122.30. The record is already unwinding.
